translationRepairs: Zhang Ling, style name Maoting, of the Sartu clan, a man of the Mongol Plain White Banner; son of Minister Nayantai and younger brother of Hui Ling.
Chang Ling, style name Maoting, of the Sartu clan, a man of the Mongol Plain White Banner; son of Minister Nayantai and younger brother of Hui Ling.
The biography opens with 長齡; here 長 is Chang, not the surname Zhang, matching the idiomatic rendering Chang Ling.

In the fifth year he went to Hubei to suppress the sect rebels, served as expeditionary grand secretary, repeatedly defeated Gao Tiansheng and Ma Xueli at the Sichuan-Hubei border, and was appointed commander of Yichang Garrison.

In the fifth year he went to Hubei to suppress the sect rebels, served as expeditionary commissioner, repeatedly defeated Gao Tiansheng and Ma Xueli at the Sichuan-Hubei border, and was appointed commander of Yichang Garrison.
領隊大臣 is an expeditionary/banner-leading commissioner; 大學士 is the office of grand secretary, which the Chinese does not use here.
In the third year (1823) he was appointed a Grand Council minister, placed in charge of the Ministry of Revenue's three treasuries, and served as chief interpreter.
In the third year (1823) he was appointed a Grand Council minister, placed in charge of the Ministry of Revenue's three treasuries, and served as chief anda.
總諳達 is the chief anda (Manchu companion-tutor of princes), not an interpreter.
In the third year he was appointed Grand Council minister, placed in charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, and served as chief interpreter.
In the third year he was appointed Grand Council minister, placed in charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, and served as chief anda.
The same 總諳達 in the literal field is chief anda, not chief interpreter.
Zhang Ling memorialized: "The rebel chieftain has already occupied his lair, and the whole situation is stirring.
Chang Ling memorialized: "The rebel chieftain has already occupied his lair, and the whole situation is stirring.
The memorialist is 長齡 (Chang Ling); Zhang Ling misreads 長 as the surname Zhang.
An edict appointed Zhang Ling Pacification General, with Yuchun and Shandong Governor Wulong'a as deputies, to lead the armies in suppressing the rebels.
An edict appointed Chang Ling Yangwei General (General of Manifested Might), with Yuchun and Shandong Governor Wulong'a as deputies, to lead the armies in suppressing the rebels.
長齡 is Chang Ling, and 揚威將軍 is the Yangwei (Manifested Might) generalship, not a generic Pacification General.

By then Provincial Commander Dalin'a and others had already defeated the rebels at the Hunbash River. Jahangir Khoja held Korla with three thousand men, and Provincial Commander Yang Fang was ordered to attack and rout them.

By then Provincial Commander Dalin'a and others had already defeated the rebels at the Hunbash River. Jahangir Khoja held Korping with three thousand men, and Provincial Commander Yang Fang was ordered to attack and rout them.
柯爾坪 is Korping/Kelpin; Korla is 庫爾勒, a different place.

At that time Provincial Commander Dalin'a and others had already defeated the rebels at the Hunbash River; Zhangge'er held Korla with three thousand men, and Provincial Commander Yang Fang was ordered to attack and break them.

At that time Provincial Commander Dalin'a and others had already defeated the rebels at the Hunbash River; Zhangge'er held Korping with three thousand men, and Provincial Commander Yang Fang was ordered to attack and break them.
The literal field likewise misidentifies 柯爾坪 as Korla; Korping is the place named.

The emperor sharply rebuked the error of their request to release the rebel scion, stripped them of office but kept them on duty, and appointed Na Yancheng Imperial Commissioner to replace Zhang Ling in planning postwar arrangements.

The emperor sharply rebuked the error of their request to release the rebel scion, stripped them of office but kept them on duty, and appointed Na Yancheng Imperial Commissioner to replace Chang Ling in planning postwar arrangements.
那彥成 is appointed to replace 長齡 (Chang Ling), not Zhang Ling.
Zhang Ling and others sent loyal Black Muslims to lure him; he led five hundred infantry and cavalry, intending to strike Kashgar on New Year's Eve.
Chang Ling and others sent loyal Black Muslims to lure him; he led five hundred infantry and cavalry, intending to strike Kashgar on New Year's Eve.
The agents who sent the lure are 長齡等; Chang Ling, not Zhang Ling.

In the first month of the eighth year news of victory arrived; the emperor was greatly pleased and enfeoffed Zhang Ling as Duke Weiyong of the second rank, hereditary in perpetuity, granted the jeweled finial, four-clawed dragon surcoat, and purple bridle, and appointed him Grand Minister in Attendance.

In the first month of the eighth year news of victory arrived; the emperor was greatly pleased and enfeoffed Chang Ling as Duke Weiyong of the second rank, hereditary in perpetuity, granted the jeweled finial, four-clawed dragon surcoat, and purple bridle, and appointed him Grand Minister in Attendance.
The duke is 長齡; Chang Ling, not Zhang Ling.
Zhang Ling was advanced to Grand Guardian, granted the triple-eyed peacock feather, and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
Chang Ling was advanced to Grand Guardian, granted the triple-eyed peacock feather, and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
The honors are conferred on 長齡 (Chang Ling).
Zhang Ling was again appointed Pacification General and sent to supervise the army.
Chang Ling was again appointed Yangwei General (General of Manifested Might) and sent to supervise the army.
長齡 is Chang Ling, but the line still calls 揚威將軍 a Pacification General; that title is Yangwei General.

Meanwhile Yarkand Commissioner Bichang repeatedly defeated the rebels; Zhang Ling ordered Deputy Hal'a and Provincial Commander Hu Chao to advance by separate routes to relieve Kashgar and Yengisar, and the rebels, hearing the news, lifted the siege and fled beyond the passes.

Meanwhile Yarkand Commissioner Bichang repeatedly defeated the rebels; Chang Ling ordered Deputy Hal'a and Provincial Commander Hu Chao to advance by separate routes to relieve Kashgar and Yengisar, and the rebels, hearing the news, lifted the siege and fled beyond the passes.
The commander issuing orders is 長齡 (Chang Ling), not Zhang Ling.

After two years on the Muslim frontier, in the twelfth year Chang Ling returned to Beijing, was promoted to Grand Preceptor, put in charge of the Board of War, transferred to the Board of Revenue, and granted a four-clawed dragon robe.

After two years on the Muslim frontier, in the twelfth year Chang Ling returned to Beijing, was promoted to Grand Preceptor, put in charge of the Board of War, transferred to the Board of Revenue, and granted a four-slit court robe.
四開褉袍 is a four-slit court robe, not a four-clawed dragon robe (四爪龍袍).

Chang Ling had garrisoned the Muslim frontier for two years in all; in the twelfth year he returned to the capital, was advanced to Grand Preceptor, managed the Board of War, was transferred to the Board of Revenue, and was granted a four-clawed dragon robe.

Chang Ling had garrisoned the Muslim frontier for two years in all; in the twelfth year he returned to the capital, was advanced to Grand Preceptor, managed the Board of War, was transferred to the Board of Revenue, and was granted a four-slit court robe.
The literal field makes the same error: 四開褉袍 names slits in the robe, not dragon claws.

In the seventh year he went to Jiangxi to investigate the impeachment of Governor Zhang Chengji, the case still undecided; when Guangdong Governor-General Jiqing, censured for suppressing secret-society bandits, committed suicide, Na Yancheng was ordered to conduct the inquest.

In the seventh year he went to Jiangxi to investigate the impeachment of Governor Zhang Chengji, the case still undecided; when Liangguang Governor-General Jiqing, censured for suppressing secret-society bandits, committed suicide, Na Yancheng was ordered to conduct the inquest.
兩廣總督 is the governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi (Liangguang), not Guangdong alone.

In the eighteenth year Li Wencheng and other Tiandihui rebels in Henan rose in revolt, seized Huaxian, and drew responses from Zhili and Shandong; Lin Qing mustered followers and attacked the Forbidden Gate.

In the eighteenth year Li Wencheng and other Heavenly Principle (Tianli) sect rebels in Henan rose in revolt, seized Huaxian, and drew responses from Zhili and Shandong; Lin Qing mustered followers and attacked the Forbidden Gate.
天理會 is the Tianli (Heavenly Principle) teaching of 1813, not the Tiandihui (天地會).
In the eighteenth year Henan Tiandihui sect rebels led by Li Wencheng and others rose, seized Huaxian, and Zhili and Shandong all responded; Lin Qing gathered a party and attacked the Forbidden Gate.
In the eighteenth year Henan Tianli sect rebels led by Li Wencheng and others rose, seized Huaxian, and Zhili and Shandong all responded; Lin Qing gathered a party and attacked the Forbidden Gate.
The literal field likewise confuses 天理會 with the Tiandihui; Tianli is the sect named.
He drove tribes that had encroached north of the Yellow River back to their original pastures in Henan, tightened regulations, and suppressed Han collaborators, and the region gradually calmed.

He drove tribes that had privately settled north of the Yellow River back to their original pastures south of the river, tightened regulations, and suppressed Han collaborators, and the region gradually calmed.
In this Qinghai passage 河北/河南 are the north and south banks of the Yellow River, not Henan province; 私住 is unauthorized settlement.
Restored to service, he served as commander of Mulan Garrison.
Restored to service, he served as commander of Malan Garrison.
馬蘭鎮 is Malan Garrison at the Eastern Qing tombs, not Mulan (木蘭).
Restored, he served as commander at Mulan Garrison.
Restored, he served as commander at Malan Garrison.
The literal field repeats the same misreading of 馬蘭鎮 as Mulan.
As guardsman he accompanied Commissioner Yijing in the defense of Guangdong.
As guardsman he accompanied Yangwei General Yijing in the defense of Guangdong.
揚威將軍奕經 bears the Yangwei generalship; Commissioner erases that title.
As guardsman he followed the Expel-Awry General Yijing in defending Guangdong.
As guardsman he followed Yangwei General Yijing in defending Guangdong.
Expel-Awry is a false calque of 揚威; the title is Yangwei General.
He served as resident commissioner at Urga and again as commander of Mulan Garrison.
He served as resident commissioner at Urga and again as commander of Malan Garrison.
復為馬蘭鎮總兵 again names Malan Garrison, not Mulan.
Served as resident commissioner at Urga and again as commander at Mulan Garrison.
Served as resident commissioner at Urga and again as commander at Malan Garrison.
The literal field again misreads 馬蘭鎮 as Mulan.
He served as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretariat academician.
He served as Chancellor of the Supervisorate of Instruction and Grand Secretariat academician.
詹事 is the chancellor of the Supervisorate of Instruction, not 太子少保 (Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent).
Served as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretariat academician.
Served as Chancellor of the Supervisorate of Instruction and Grand Secretariat academician.
The literal field makes the same substitution of Junior Guardian for 詹事.
He entered the Southern Study attached to the throne room.
He entered duty in the Shangshufang (the palace school).
上書房 is the Shangshufang (palace school for princes), not the Southern Study (南書房).
Entered the Southern Study attached to the throne room.
上書房 is the Shangshufang, but the proposed line still invents “attached to the throne room,” which the Chinese does not say.
In the seventh year he became Hanlin Academy chancellor and chief tutor of the Southern Study and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
In the seventh year he became Hanlin Academy chancellor and chief tutor of the Shangshufang and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
上書房總師傅 is chief tutor of the Shangshufang, not of the Southern Study.
In the seventh year, concurrently Hanlin Academy chancellor, chief tutor of the Southern Study, made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
In the seventh year, concurrently Hanlin Academy chancellor, chief tutor of the Shangshufang, made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
The literal field likewise renders 上書房 as the Southern Study.

In the eighteenth year (1813) he followed Na Yancheng against the Huaxian sect rebels, fought fiercely and repeatedly defeated them, captured Sizhai, destroyed the chief rebel Li Wencheng, took Huacheng, seized rebel leaders, and was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

In the eighteenth year (1813) he followed Na Yancheng against the Huaxian sect rebels, fought fiercely and repeatedly defeated them, captured Sizhai, destroyed the chief rebel Li Wencheng, took Huaxian, seized rebel leaders, and was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
克滑縣 is the taking of Huaxian (滑縣), already named earlier in the sentence; Huacheng is not a place here.

In the eighteenth year he followed Na Yancheng in suppressing the sect rebels at Huaxian, fought fiercely, repeatedly defeated the rebels, captured Sizhai, destroyed the chief rebel Li Wencheng, captured Huacheng, seized rebel leaders, and was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

In the eighteenth year he followed Na Yancheng in suppressing the sect rebels at Huaxian, fought fiercely, repeatedly defeated the rebels, captured Sizhai, destroyed the chief rebel Li Wencheng, captured Huaxian, seized rebel leaders, and was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
The literal field likewise turns the second 滑縣 into Huacheng instead of Huaxian.
As frontier colonies around Balchuan gradually prospered, garrison troops were judiciously reduced.
As frontier colonies around Barchuk gradually prospered, garrison troops were judiciously reduced.
巴爾楚克 is the Kashgar-route oasis Barchuk, not Balchuan.
Frontier colonies in Balchuan and other places gradually flourished, and garrison troops were judiciously reduced.
Frontier colonies in Barchuk and other places gradually flourished, and garrison troops were judiciously reduced.
The literal field repeats the same misrendering of 巴爾楚克 as Balchuan.
